# their_thing: cuml ML::Solver::Lars (cpp/src/solver/lars_impl.cuh), the CALLER of choleskyRank1Update
why / where it would go: LARS is a solver section, not a Cholesky one. It is named here because the brief that opened this lane said cuML's SVM uses the rank-one update and the checkout says otherwise: grep -rn cholesky cuml/cpp/src/svm/ at 265b9da returns nothing, and cuML's SVM solver is SMO. PORTING_RULES rule 1 -- the file wins, and the false sentence is deleted rather than annotated

their test compares updateCholesky against cusolverDnpotrf at a tolerance, which is the right test for a library shipping one backend and says nothing this lane needs. cholesky/checks/cholesky_check.mojo's check_r1_update_equals_potrf is the same comparison made BITWISE and between two of our own device spellings

# their_thing: a BLOCKED trsm (the shape cublastrsm actually uses)
why / where it would go: cholesky/checks/trsm.mojo is one thread per right-hand-side column with no reuse of L. A blocked trsm turns the solve into GEMM work; it is a speed idea, it would introduce a second fold to pin, and this lane has measured nothing. cholesky/README.md carries it under WHAT IS OWED

# their_thing: a panel factorization staged in threadgroup memory
why / where it would go: same reason (DEVIATION 1641): a staging tile is a page count to pin, and a second thing to pin is a second thing to get wrong

# their_thing: cublasSsyrk (the symmetric rank-k update a real blocked Cholesky uses for its trailing update)
status: NOT PORTED -- CLOSED, AND THE SHAPE IS NOT IN THE GEMM PROFILE
why / where it would go: DEVIATION 1636 computes the full n_trail x n_trail product with identical_gemm_into at OP_NT and subtracts only the lower triangle, doing twice the FLOPs. A triangular output shape would need a new arm of mojolearn.identical.gemm.fp32.v1 or a hand-written contraction here, and both are worse than twice the FLOPs in a lane with no published number
